taxonomy:
# Taxonomy of Grid-Based Logic Puzzles

## I. By Primary Task Type

### A. Loop/Path Drawing
Puzzles where the solver draws a single continuous loop or path through the grid.

#### A1. Pure Loop Construction
- **Masyu** – Loop through cells, constrained by black/white circle rules
- **Slitherlink** – Loop on grid edges (dots), constrained by number clues
- **Mid-loop** – Loop through cells, black circles must be midpoints of straight segments
- **Nagareru** – Directed loop with wind constraints
- **Moon-or-Sun** – Loop through rooms, alternating between moon/sun symbols
- **Suraromu** – Loop starting/ending at numbered circle, passing through all gates in order
- **Dotchi-Loop** – Loop through cells, with straight/turn constraints per region based on white circles; avoids black circles

#### A2. Loop with Shading
- **Yajilin** – Loop plus placement of black cells, with directional number clues

#### A3. Path/Connection Drawing
- **Numberlink** – Connect pairs of identical numbers with non-crossing paths
- **Hashiwokakero** – Connect islands (numbered circles) with bridges (1 or 2 per pair), forming a connected network

---

### B. Cell Shading/Painting
Puzzles where the solver colors certain cells black (or leaves them white).

#### B1. Shading with Number Clues (counting adjacent/nearby black cells)
- **Kurotto** – Numbers in circles indicate sum of sizes of orthogonally adjacent black groups
- **Akari** – Place light bulbs; numbers on black squares count adjacent bulbs; illumination and visibility constraints
- **Usowan** – Numbers count adjacent colored cells, but exactly one number per bold-lined region is wrong
- **Nurikabe** – Numbers indicate size of white islands; black cells form one connected wall with no 2×2 blocks

#### B2. Shading with Connectivity/Shape Constraints
- **Heyawake** – Shading in rooms with number clues; no adjacent black cells; white cells connected; white cells can't span more than two rooms in a line
- **Kurodoko** – Numbers count visible white cells in four directions; black cells non-adjacent; white cells connected
- **Norinori** – Exactly two black cells per bold-lined region; all black cells in dominoes (pairs)
- **LITS** – Place one tetromino per region; same-shape tetrominoes non-adjacent; all colored cells connected; no 2×2 black squares
- **Nurimisaki** – Circle cells are white "promontories" (one white neighbor); numbers indicate length of white line; no 2×2 of either color; white connected
- **Nuritwin** – Each region has exactly two same-sized shaded blocks; all shaded cells globally connected; blocks in same region don't touch; no 2×2 shading
- **Nurimeizu** – Shade entire rooms to create a maze from S to G; circle rooms on shortest path, triangle rooms not; no 2×2 of either color; white connected without loops

#### B3. Shading with Rectangular/Shape Formation Constraints
- **Choco Banana** – Black groups must form rectangles/squares; white groups must NOT form rectangles/squares; numbers indicate area size
- **Shakashaka** – Place triangles in cells so remaining white areas form rectangles/squares; numbers count adjacent triangles
- **Tilepaint** – Color entire tiles (bold-lined regions); diagonal-cell clues count black cells in row/column segments

#### B4. Shading with Gravity/Physical Constraints
- **Sto-stone** – Shade cells in rooms (number = count of black cells per room); black cells don't connect across room borders; when "dropped" they fill bottom half of grid

---

### C. Number/Symbol Placement
Puzzles where the solver fills cells with numbers or symbols.

#### C1. Latin Square Variants
- **Sudoku** – Place 1–9 in each row, column, and 3×3 box
- **Hitori** – Eliminate duplicate numbers by shading; no adjacent black cells; white cells connected

#### C2. Region-Based Number Fill
- **Fillomino** – Fill grid with numbers; groups of same number form blocks of that size; same-sized blocks can't be orthogonally adjacent
- **Ripple Effect** – Fill rooms with 1 to N; same numbers in a row/column must be spaced apart by at least the number's value
- **Makaro** – Fill rooms with 1 to N; arrow cells point to the largest neighbor; same numbers can't be adjacent across rooms
- **Nansuke** – Fill blank cells with digits from a given number list, placing multi-digit numbers left-to-right or top-to-bottom

#### C3. Symbol/Mark Placement
- **Juosan** – Fill every cell with — or |; territory numbers constrain the difference in counts; runs of same symbol limited in perpendicular direction
- **Hebi** – Place snakes (numbered 1–5) in white cells with adjacency, visibility, and directional constraints

---

### D. Grid Division/Partitioning
Puzzles where the solver divides the grid into regions or blocks.

#### D1. Rectangular Partitioning
- **Shikaku** – Divide grid into rectangles, each containing exactly one number equal to its area

#### D2. Fixed-Size Partitioning
- **Five Cells** – Divide grid into pentominoes (blocks of 5); numbers count surrounding block edges (including outer frame)

#### D3. Shape-Constrained Partitioning
- **Sashigane** – Divide grid into L-shaped blocks; circles mark bends; arrows mark ends pointing toward bends; numbers indicate block size
- **Double Choco** – Divide grid into blocks each containing matching white and gray sub-regions of identical shape; numbers indicate half-block size

#### D4. Partitioning with Evolutionary/Sequential Constraints
- **Evolomino** – Place square markers forming blocks; each arrow passes through blocks that grow by one cell sequentially without rotation

---

### E. Object Placement/Movement
Puzzles where the solver places or moves discrete objects.

#### E1. Placement
- **Akari** – Place light bulbs in white cells (also in Shading category due to illumination)
- **Pencils** – Identify pencil shapes and draw lines from tips; numbers indicate pencil length and line length

#### E2. Movement
- **Satogaeri** – Move numbered circles within countries so each country has exactly one; numbers indicate distance moved; paths can't cross
- **Yosenabe** – Move all circles into gray areas via straight arrows; arrows can't cross or pass through other circles; gray area numbers equal sum of entering circle values

---

### F. Block/Chain Formation
Puzzles focused on forming and constraining groups of black cells.

- **Chained Block** – Form black-cell blocks; numbers indicate block size; every block must be part of a chain (corner-touching); no duplicate size/shape within a chain

---

## II. Cross-Cutting Dimensions

### By Constraint Type

| Constraint | Puzzles |
|---|---|
| **Connectivity of white cells** | Hitori, Heyawake, Kurodoko, Nurikabe, Nurimisaki, Usowan, Nurimeizu |
| **Connectivity of black/shaded cells** | LITS, Nurikabe, Nuritwin, Sto-stone |
| **No 2×2 block of same color** | Nurikabe, LITS, Nurimisaki, Nuritwin, Nurimeizu, Sto-stone |
| **No adjacent black cells** | Heyawake, Hitori, Kurodoko, Usowan, Yajilin, Norinori (except within dominoes) |
| **Directional/arrow clues** | Yajilin, Makaro, Hebi, Yosenabe, Sashigane, Pencils, Nagareru |
| **Room/region constraints** | Heyawake, Makaro, Ripple Effect, Five Cells, Double Choco, Moon-or-Sun, Nurimeizu, Nuritwin, Dotchi-Loop, Suraromu, Usowan |
| **Counting clues (adjacent)** | Akari, Kurotto, Shakashaka, Slitherlink, Five Cells, Usowan |
| **Counting clues (line-of-sight/visibility)** | Kurodoko, Nurimisaki, Akari, Yajilin, Hebi |
| **Shape matching/congruence** | Double Choco, Chained Block, LITS, Nuritwin |
| **Single loop** | Masyu, Slitherlink, Mid-loop, Nagareru, Moon-or-Sun, Suraromu, Yajilin, Dotchi-Loop |
| **Movement/displacement** | Satogaeri, Yosenabe |
| **Deception (one wrong clue)** | Usowan |
| **Gravity/dropping** | Sto-stone |
